review: Sender/receiver arrows, key ownership, confidentiality boundary and firewall decisions visually reviewed. Exact numerical diagrams are generated separately as SVG.

entries.prompt: Create one precise educational infographic for a Cambridge AS Computer Science lesson: DIGITAL SIGNATURE: AUTHENTICATE A MESSAGE. Landscape 3:2, clean white background, navy headings, teal sender steps, blue receiver steps, orange final comparison, ample whitespace. Crisp English text, no logos. Two clearly separated lanes SENDER and RECEIVER, large readable labels. Sender sequence: 'Message' -> 'Hash algorithm' -> 'Digest' -> 'Sign with sender’s private key' -> 'Digital signature'. A transmission arrow labelled 'Send message + signature' connects lanes. Receiver uses received Message -> 'Same hash algorithm' -> 'New digest'. Separately 'Received signature' + 'Sender’s public key' -> 'Verify signature'. Show comparison of the new digest with the signed digest/evidence leading to 'Match: evidence of origin and unchanged content'. Footer exact text: 'Signing does not hide the message. Encryption protects confidentiality.' Conceptual educational signing model; do not say the whole message is encrypted or that the public key is secret. Do not depict an arbitrary checksum as a secure hash. Only these concepts, no added text or numeric examples. All arrow flows must be unambiguous; sender private key stays sender side. Polished textbook diagram with small document and key pictograms.
entries.revisionPrompt: Correct the attached digital-signature educational infographic, keeping its palette, crisp typography, title and footer. Redraw the wiring with these exact constraints. 1) REMOVE the vertical line that descends from the sender Digest box, and REMOVE the arrow into the receiver New digest box from above. No digest is sent separately. 2) The transmission panel 'Send message + signature' is a standalone labelled divider with NO arrows connecting it to any node; it describes the transfer generally. 3) In RECEIVER bottom row, move 'Received signature' to x approximately 80, 'Sender’s public key' to below it if necessary, then draw TWO independent distinct arrows from these two boxes into 'Verify signature'. Do not draw two arrows from the public key. 'Received signature' MUST have its own connected arrow into Verify signature. 4) Receiver upper row is only Received Message -> Same hash algorithm -> New digest -> final comparison. 5) Receiver lower row is Received signature plus Sender’s public key -> Verify signature -> Signed digest (evidence) -> final comparison. Keep all nodes and arrows separated, no overlapping text. Sender upper row remains Message -> Hash algorithm -> Digest -> Sign with sender’s private key -> Digital signature. Keep English wording and footnote. This is a precise repair, not a new topic.

entries.prompt: Create a precise educational flow infographic, landscape 3:2, clean navy/teal/blue textbook style on white, very readable English labels. Title 'ENCRYPTION PROTECTS CONFIDENTIALITY'. Show a left-to-right main chain with generous spaces: a readable document labelled 'Plaintext' -> green box labelled 'Encryption algorithm + key' -> scrambled document labelled 'Ciphertext' -> blue box labelled 'Decryption algorithm + correct key' -> readable document labelled 'Recovered plaintext'. Under the ciphertext ONLY show a branch down to an interceptor pictogram with exact caption 'Intercepted copy: unreadable without the required key'. Beneath the main chain show two separately labelled compact panels: 'Encryption' with 'Protects the contents of a stolen or intercepted copy'; 'Access rights' with 'Control who may read, modify or delete a stored file'. Footer: 'These controls perform different jobs and can be used together.' No numerical ciphers, no promise of absolute security, no implication encryption stops deletion, no digital signatures or biometrics. Make every arrow connect only the described sequential stages. Use visual document/lock/key icons rather than walls of text. No logos, no border crop.

Create a textbook educational diagram titled 'A FIREWALL FILTERS TRAFFIC'. White background, navy type, teal allow arrows, orange blocked arrows, landscape 3:2, crisp readable English labels and small computer/network icons. Main large visual: Internet on left -> 'Firewall: compare traffic with configured rules' central rule panel -> 'Protected network' with server and two computers on right. Incoming examples clearly labelled 'Allowed connection' passes along teal arrow through firewall into network; 'Disallowed connection' ends at orange stop symbol AT the firewall, no arrow past it. Include a clearly labelled return path 'Outgoing traffic is checked too' travelling from protected network back toward Internet through firewall. Below, two distinct small diagrams: 'Host firewall: protects one computer' with firewall boundary around one PC; 'Network firewall: filters traffic at the network boundary' with firewall before a LAN of devices. Footer 'A firewall reduces risk; it does not replace authentication, anti-malware or careful user decisions.' Avoid implying all malware is detected. No checklists of syllabus terms, no arbitrary port values, no digital signatures, no logos, no decorative filler. Prioritise unambiguous arrows and legibility.
